Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
5 October 2026 .
Brent $ 100.20 -2.58 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Iran says the strait will not reopen until conditions are met; Iraq's state tanker firm reports it is moving crude through the strait, leaving the physical transit picture contested.

02 Brent stood at $100.20, down 2.58% over 24 hours, as of 20:46 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
Who has carried out the strikes remains attributed rather than settled: UKMTO, per Rudaw, has flagged three tanker incidents in 24 hours and describes the weapon in at least one case as an unknown projectile. The product tanker Lipsi, hit on October 4, was named separately by Data Portuaria as the vessel struck by a projectile in the strait. The closure and transit picture remains contested: Iran says the strait will not reopen until its conditions are met, while Iraq's state tanker firm reports it is moving crude through the strait. Kuwait, per gCaptain, is pumping at roughly 75% of pre-war output. The BBC reports Saudi-backed Yemeni forces have retaken Mokha and secured the Bab al-Mandab Strait, removing Houthi control of that chokepoint. Brent was at $100.20, down 2.58% over 24 hours, as of 20:46 UTC. The site recorded 52 indexed events in the past 24 hours. As of 20:50 UTC, 241 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, rising over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
